run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The social-network frontend pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 is crash-looping: its nginx-thrift container runs with requests/limits memory 16Mi (its own ReplicaSet template and Deployment declare 128Mi/256Mi), it was OOMKilled with exit code 137 at 2026-11-21T12:10:30Z, and by 12:11:42Z it was Ready=false with restartCount 3 and state CrashLoopBackOff. Its Service nginx-thrift has only that pod listed as a notReadyAddress, so the frontend has no ready backend. The 16Mi value is held in ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server (MEMORY = "16Mi", applied to container[0] requests/limits by a JSON-patch admission handler); that handler is served by Deployment platform-policy-controller in platform-ops and was wired to five MutatingWebhookConfigurations created at 12:10:15Z that target pods created in namespace social-network. The failing pod was created at 12:10:23Z, after those webhooks existed, and is the only pod in the cluster carrying a 16Mi limit, so the evidence points to the admission mutation as the mechanism that replaced the workload's declared memory limit and caused the OOM kill. All other 26 social-network pods were Running/ready with restartCount 0 and no memory limits, and the sampled spans from the other services carried no error status. Because the webhook's own log is empty and no audit record of the admission response was available, the mutation of this specific pod is supported by the template discrepancy plus the webhook program code rather than observed directly; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: Pod social-network/nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 (created 2026-11-21T12:10:23Z) runs container nginx-thrift with requests.memory=16Mi and limits.memory=16Mi; that container was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 (startedAt 12:10:25Z, finishedAt 12:10:30Z), and at 12:11:42Z the pod reported Ready=False (reason ContainersNotReady), restartCount 3 and container state waiting/CrashLoopBackOff with last termination exitCode 137 and reason Error (startedAt 12:11:16Z, finishedAt 12:11:19Z).

The nginx-thrift workload template does not declare 16Mi: Deployment nginx-thrift (namespace social-network, generation 2, revision 2) declares container nginx-thrift requests.memory=128Mi and limits.memory=256Mi, and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 (created 12:09:57Z, owner Deployment nginx-thrift) declares the same 128Mi/256Mi, while its pod carries 16Mi.

ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server (created 2026-11-21T12:10:12Z) contains key server.py whose setting MEMORY = "16Mi" is written by build_patch() into /spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory and /spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory of every admitted pod (JSONPatch, allowed=True), replacing existing values when present.

Deployment platform-ops/platform-policy-controller (created 2026-11-21T12:10:12Z) runs command ["python","/app/server.py"] from configMap volume platform-policy-controller-server and listens on containerPort 8443; Service platform-policy-controller in platform-ops exposes port 443 to targetPort 8443 with selector app=platform-policy-controller.

Five MutatingWebhookConfigurations (cert-manager-webhook, gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration, istio-sidecar-injector, kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg, linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config) all carry creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:10:15Z and every one sends clientConfig.service platform-policy-controller (namespace platform-ops, path /mutate, port 443); the gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration webhook mutation.gatekeeper.sh has rules apiGroups [""] / apiVersions v1 / resources pods / operations CREATE, failurePolicy Fail, and namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name=social-network.

nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 is the only pod in namespace social-network created after 12:10:15Z (created 12:10:23Z), and it is the only pod in the whole cluster whose container declares limits.memory=16Mi.

Service nginx-thrift (ClusterIP, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector service=nginx-thrift) has an Endpoints object whose single subset lists pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 at 10.244.234.142 only under notReadyAddresses, i.e. the frontend Service had no ready backend at 12:12:35Z.

Events for namespace social-network record: pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 Scheduled at 12:10:23Z, Warning BackOff at 12:10:34Z "Back-off restarting failed container nginx-thrift in pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7_social-network", pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-j2xch Killing at 12:10:23Z, ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 SuccessfulCreate of both j2xch (12:09:57Z) and q5dz7 (12:10:23Z), and pod nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df-wrp98 SuccessfulDelete at 12:10:11Z with Deployment nginx-thrift scaling replica set nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df from 1 to 0.

The 156 spans returned for service nginx-web-server in the 12:00:00-12:10:35Z window cover 12:10:04.009Z-12:10:23.156Z; in the 80 rows read, the /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read server spans carry http.status_code=200 and no error tag or error detail.

At 12:10:35Z the cumulative span counter existed for all 12 social-network services (nginx-web-server 78, user-timeline-service 40, home-timeline-service 31, post-storage-service 27, compose-post-service 8, others <=3 per service, summed over that service's span_name series), showing the frontend was still exporting spans during its last running minute.

All other 26 pods in namespace social-network were phase Running with every container ready=true and restartCount 0 at 12:10:37Z, and their container specs declare no memory requests or limits (resources {}).

At 12:10:35Z kube-state-metrics reported kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready=1 for all 27 deployments in social-network, including nginx-thrift, while the nginx-thrift pod itself was unready and OOM-killed at 12:10:30Z and later CrashLoopBackOff; deployment-level readiness therefore lagged and does not show this fault, so pod-level state is the reliable signal here.

The ConfigMaps inside namespace social-network hold only application configuration keys (jaeger-config.yml, service-config.json, nginx.conf, redis.conf, mongod.conf), so no in-namespace setting carrying a 16Mi memory limit was seen; the 16Mi value is held outside the application namespace in platform-ops.

The crash-loop is caused by the platform-policy-controller admission handler, which stamped the 16Mi MEMORY value over the 256Mi limit declared by ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 when pod q5dz7 was created at 12:10:23Z (after the webhooks appeared at 12:10:15Z); 16Mi was too small for openresty-thrift and the container was killed by the kernel OOM killer, reproducing as CrashLoopBackOff.

Pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-j2xch was deleted by something outside its ReplicaSet at 12:10:23Z (only a Killing event exists for it, with no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete) and the ReplicaSet then created q5dz7, which forced the new pod through the admission path that applied 16Mi.

Any future pod created in namespace social-network will receive the same 16Mi memory limit, because the gatekeeper-mutating-webhook-configuration pod-CREATE rule matches the social-network namespace and the handler always patches container[0] memory; today only nginx-thrift was recreated, so the other services still run with no memory limits.

The 16Mi limit was not an intended value of the nginx-thrift workload: both the Deployment template (generation 2) and ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-65f656c999 declare 128Mi requests / 256Mi limits, and the older ReplicaSet nginx-thrift-68bc7d94df declared no resources at all, so 16Mi never appears in any workload template observed.

The missing frontend backend is not a Service selector mismatch: the nginx-thrift Service selector service=nginx-thrift does match the failing pod, since that pod is listed (as a notReadyAddress) in the Service's own Endpoints object.

Human follow-up: change or remove MEMORY = "16Mi" in ConfigMap platform-ops/platform-policy-controller-server (or disable the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations that point at platform-policy-controller) and have the nginx-thrift pod recreated, then confirm the new pod keeps limits.memory=256Mi / requests.memory=128Mi and that Service nginx-thrift has a ready endpoint again.

gaps: The admission response for pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-q5dz7 was not observed directly: the platform-policy-controller container returned no log lines (its log_message handler is suppressed in server.py) and no audit/admission record was available, so applying 16Mi to this specific pod is inferred from the pod-vs-ReplicaSet template discrepancy plus the webhook program code.

I cannot tell whether the MEMORY="16Mi" value was edited after ConfigMap platform-policy-controller-server was created at 2026-11-21T12:10:12Z; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

What deleted pod nginx-thrift-65f656c999-j2xch at 12:10:23Z, and who changed Deployment nginx-thrift to revision 2 (resources 128Mi/256Mi) at 12:09:57Z, is not shown by any event or object I retrieved.

Prometheus kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="social-network"} > 0 returned no series at 12:10:35Z, so restart counts from metrics are unknown; the restart count of 3 comes from the pod's status at 12:11:42Z.

No traces for nginx-web-server later than 12:10:23.156Z were returned for the 12:00-12:10:35Z window, and the trace sample is biased, so the frontend request error rate or the number of failed requests after the OOM kill is not quantified.
Every trace status_code label value observed for these services is STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so no span error-status metric exists here to compute an error rate for the affected or unaffected services.
Cluster-wide NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota queries returned no objects; their absence as a contributing factor is not confirmed.
End-user/downstream impact beyond the missing ready endpoint of Service nginx-thrift (e.g. HTTP failures seen by callers) is unverified.

Events in namespace observe (Pod Unhealthy, Pod FailedScheduling, StatefulSet FailedUpdate) belong to the monitoring stack and were not investigated in depth; they are not tied to this fault by evidence.
next_steps: Inspect the five MutatingWebhookConfigurations and Deployment platform-policy-controller in platform-ops, and replace the 16Mi MEMORY constant with the workload's real requirement or remove the pod mutation entirely.

After the fix, recreate the nginx-thrift pod and verify its container resources match the ReplicaSet template (128Mi requests / 256Mi limits), that it stays Ready beyond several minutes, and that Endpoints for Service nginx-thrift lists a ready address.
Enable admission/audit logging for the webhook so future mutations of pods in namespace social-network can be observed directly rather than inferred.
Review whether other namespaces are meant to be excluded from the platform-policy-controller webhooks, since the current rule targets all pod CREATE operations in social-network.

import base64
import json
import ssl
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

MEMORY = "16Mi"

def build_patch(resources):
    """Emit JSON Patch ops that stamp MEMORY into both
    resources.requests.memory and resources.limits.memory on container[0].
    RFC 6902 "add" semantics: replaces the value if the target already exists,
    so this works whether the field is absent or already populated."""
    ops = []
    if resources is None:
        ops.append({
            "op": "add",
            "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources",
            "value": {"requests": {"memory": MEMORY}, "limits": {"memory": MEMORY}},
        })
        return ops
    if resources.get("requests") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    if resources.get("limits") is None:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits",
                    "value": {"memory": MEMORY}})
    else:
        ops.append({"op": "add", "path": "/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory",
                    "value": MEMORY})
    return ops

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0") or 0)
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        uid = ""
        patch = []
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
            uid = body.get("request", {}).get("uid", "")
            containers = body.get("request", {}).get("object", {}).get("spec", {}).get("containers", [])
            if containers:
                patch = build_patch(containers[0].get("resources"))
        except Exception:
            pass

        resp = {"uid": uid, "allowed": True}
        if patch:
            resp["patchType"] = "JSONPatch"
            resp["patch"] = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(patch).encode()).decode()
        response = {
            "apiVersion": "admission.k8s.io/v1",
            "kind": "AdmissionReview",
            "response": resp,
        }
        data = json.dumps(response).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        return

httpd = HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8443), Handler)
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
ctx.load_cert_chain("/certs/tls.crt", "/certs/tls.key")
httpd.socket = ctx.wrap_socket(httpd.socket, server_side=True)
httpd.serve_forever()
